## Why the data source matters

Most taxinfo functions look up the taxonomic names of a phyloseq object in an
external database (GBIF, NCBI, Wikidata, a trait database...). Each database
follows its own **taxonomic backbone**: its own accepted names, synonyms and
spellings. A name accepted in one backbone can be a synonym, or be missing, in
another one. Names verified against TAXREF and then searched in the GBIF
backbone, for instance, silently lose part of the matches.

The rule is therefore: **verify the names with `gna_verifier_pq()` against the
same data source as the database queried downstream**, using the
`data_sources` argument (a Global Names Architecture, GNA, data source id).

The table below gives, for each function, the database it queries, the
taxonomy that database follows, and the GNA data source to use. The full list
of GNA data sources and their last update date is at
<https://verifier.globalnames.org/data_sources>.

## Use one data source per verification

`gna_verifier_pq()` uses a single data source by default (`data_sources = 1`,
Catalogue of Life). Avoid giving several ids at once: with
`data_sources = c(1, 12)`, the GNA Verifier keeps the best match of **each
name** from whichever of the two databases it comes from. The verified names
then mix two taxonomic backbones (Catalogue of Life for one taxon,
Encyclopedia of Life for another), which is exactly what we want to avoid.

To compare or keep several taxonomic verifications, chain several calls, each
with one data source and its own `col_prefix` (see below).

## The data source is recorded in the tax_table

`gna_verifier_pq()` records the data source of the best match of each taxon in
two columns named after the `currentCanonicalSimple` column they document:
`currentCanonicalSimple_dataSourceId` and
`currentCanonicalSimple_dataSourceTitleShort`. With `col_prefix`, they take
the same prefix as the other columns. The same phyloseq object can thus keep
several verifications side by side, each with its own data source:

```{r two-sources}
library(taxinfo)
data_fungi_mini_2 <- data_fungi_mini |>
  gna_verifier_pq(data_sources = 210, col_prefix = "taxref_") |>
  gna_verifier_pq(data_sources = 11, col_prefix = "gbif_")

# Columns taxref_currentCanonicalSimple and
# taxref_currentCanonicalSimple_dataSourceId (TAXREF, id 210), and
# gbif_currentCanonicalSimple and gbif_currentCanonicalSimple_dataSourceId
# (GBIF Backbone Taxonomy, id 11)
```

`check_backbone_pq()` reads these columns and tells you when the names used by
a function were verified against another backbone than the one it queries.
The functions marked "auto" in the tables (GBIF, NCBI and Wikidata functions)
run this check by themselves
when a phyloseq object is provided:

```{r check}
# Silent: names verified against the GBIF backbone, queried in the GBIF backbone
check_backbone_pq(
  data_fungi_mini_2,
  checklist = "backbone",
  taxonomic_rank = "gbif_currentCanonicalSimple"
)

# Informs: names verified against TAXREF, queried in the GBIF backbone
tax_gbif_occur_pq(
  data_fungi_mini_2,
  taxonomic_rank = "taxref_currentCanonicalSimple"
)

# Any other function: give the expected GNA data source (4 = NCBI)
check_backbone_pq(
  data_fungi_mini_2,
  expected_source = 4,
  taxonomic_rank = "gbif_currentCanonicalSimple"
)
```

## The GBIF checklist: GBIF Backbone or Catalogue of Life XR

Since rgbif 3.9.0, GBIF matches names against the **Catalogue of Life
Extended Release** (COL XR, GNA data source `13`) instead of the legacy
**GBIF Backbone Taxonomy** (GNA data source `11`). The GBIF functions of
taxinfo use the checklist set by the `taxinfo.gbif_checklist` option:

```{r option}
options(taxinfo.gbif_checklist = "backbone") # GBIF Backbone: data_sources = 11
options(taxinfo.gbif_checklist = "colxr") # COL XR: data_sources = 13
```

When the option is unset, taxinfo follows the default of the installed rgbif
(GBIF Backbone before 3.9.0, COL XR from 3.9.0 on). Two functions always use
the GBIF Backbone, because the GBIF API they rely on
(`rgbif::name_usage()`) cannot read COL XR keys: `tax_iucn_code_pq()` and
`tax_photos_pq()` (with `source = "gbif"`); their `checklist` argument
defaults to `"backbone"`. See `gbif_key_to_col()` for details on the
migration.

Note that the GNA copy of the GBIF Backbone (id `11`) was last updated in
January 2024, while COL XR (id `13`) is updated regularly: recently described
or recombined taxa are more likely to be found in COL XR.

## Which data source for which function

In the "Check" column, *auto* means that the function runs
`check_backbone_pq()` itself; *manual* means that you can run
`check_backbone_pq(physeq, expected_source = <id>)` before calling it.

### GBIF-based functions

| Function | Database queried | Name matching | GNA `data_sources` | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tax_gbif_occur_pq()` | GBIF occurrences (counts) | `taxinfo.gbif_checklist` option | `11` (backbone) or `13` (COL XR) | auto |
| `tax_gbif_alt()` | GBIF occurrences (altitude) | `taxinfo.gbif_checklist` option | `11` or `13` | auto |
| `tax_gbif_occur_coords()` | GBIF occurrences (coordinates) | `taxinfo.gbif_checklist` option | `11` or `13` | manual |
| `tax_occur_check()`, `tax_occur_check_pq()`, `tax_occur_multi_check_pq()` | GBIF occurrences around samples | `taxinfo.gbif_checklist` option | `11` or `13` | auto (`tax_occur_check_pq()`) |
| `tax_ecoregion_occur()`, `tax_ecoregion_occur_pq()`, `tax_check_ecoregion()` | GBIF occurrences + ecoregions | `taxinfo.gbif_checklist` option | `11` or `13` | auto (`tax_ecoregion_occur_pq()`) |
| `tax_harmonize_backbone_pq()` | GBIF name matching (higher ranks) | `taxinfo.gbif_checklist` option, or a local `backbone` | `11` or `13` | manual |
| `tax_crosscheck_gbif_pq()` | GNA Verifier vs GBIF name matching | GNA `data_sources` argument (default `11`) vs `taxinfo.gbif_checklist` option | compares both | (is itself a check) |
| `range_bioreg_pq()`, `plot_range_bioreg_pq()` | GBIF occurrences via gbif.range | `taxinfo.gbif_checklist` option for the name matching, installed rgbif default inside `gbif.range::get_gbif()` | `11` or `13` | manual |
| `plot_tax_gbif_pq()` | GBIF occurrences via gbif.range | `rgbif::name_backbone()` inside `gbif.range::get_gbif()`: installed rgbif default (backbone before 3.9.0, COL XR from 3.9.0) | `11` or `13` | manual |
| `tax_iucn_code_pq()` | IUCN Red List category stored by GBIF | GBIF Backbone only (`checklist = "backbone"`) | `11` | auto |
| `tax_photos_pq()` (`source = "gbif"`) | GBIF occurrence images | GBIF Backbone only (`checklist = "backbone"`) | `11` | auto |

### Other online databases

| Function | Database queried | Name matching | GNA `data_sources` | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tax_retroblast_pq()` | NCBI nucleotide (Entrez search on organism names) | NCBI Taxonomy | `4` (NCBI) | auto |
| `tax_get_wk_info_pq()`, `tax_get_wk_lang()`, `tax_get_wk_pages_info()` | Wikidata / Wikipedia | Wikidata item search on the name | `207` (Wikidata) | auto (`tax_get_wk_info_pq()`; the two others take Wikidata ids) |
| `tax_photos_pq()` (`source = "wikitaxa"`) | Wikidata / Wikimedia Commons | Wikidata item search on the name | `207` (Wikidata) | auto |
| `tax_globi_pq()` | GloBI interactions | Names sent as written; GloBI aligns names across several taxonomies (Nomer). Target taxa are verified internally with the `data_sources` argument (default `1`) | no single backbone; `1` (Catalogue of Life) is a reasonable default | -- |
| `tax_oa_pq()` | OpenAlex works | Free-text search in titles and abstracts | no backbone: use the names as used in the literature (consider synonyms) | -- |
| `tax_spores_size_pq()` | MycoDB website (<https://www.mycodb.fr/>) | Name search on the website | not documented | -- |

### Bundled or downloaded trait databases

| Function | Database | Taxonomy of the database | GNA `data_sources` | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tax_info_pq()` | Any CSV file | The one of your CSV, e.g. TAXREF for the bundled `TAXREFv18_fungi.csv` | e.g. `210` (TaxRef) for TAXREF | manual |
| `fungal_traits_guilds()` | FungalTraits (genus level) + FUNGuild | FungalTraits genera follow the Outline of Fungi, a consensus of NCBI, Index Fungorum and Tedersoo et al. (2018) | `5` (Index Fungorum) is the closest single source; when `currentCanonicalSimple` is missing, names are verified with `gna_data_sources` (default `1`) | manual |
| `tax_bioshifts_pq()` | BioShifts (range shifts) | BioShifts names are re-verified internally with `gna_verifier_pq(data_sources = )` (default `1`) before the join | the same `data_sources` as the argument of `tax_bioshifts_pq()` | manual |
| `tax_funendo_pq()` | FunEndo (fungal endophytes) | not documented; names matched verbatim | not documented | -- |
| `tax_spores_volume_pq()` | Spore traits of Aguilar-Trigueros et al. (2023) | not documented; names matched verbatim (lower case) | not documented | -- |
| `tax_bactotraits_pq()` | BactoTraits, built from BacDive (DSMZ) | BacDive strain names; matched on the rank columns (`Species`, `Genus`...), not on `gna_verifier_pq()` columns | `208` (LPSN, the DSMZ nomenclature list) is the closest source | -- |
| `tax_metatraits_pq()` | metaTraits | GTDB r220 | GTDB is **not** a GNA data source: assign your sequences with a GTDB-based reference instead of renaming them | -- |
| `tax_faprotax_pq()` | FAPROTAX | NCBI / Bergey's taxonomy; matched on the lineage columns, not on `gna_verifier_pq()` columns | `4` (NCBI) for the lineage, if you harmonise it | -- |

"not documented" means that the taxonomy followed by the database is not
stated by taxinfo; check the reference of the database before choosing a
data source.

## Summary of the most useful GNA data sources

| GNA id | Data source | Use it before |
|---|---|---|
| `1` | Catalogue of Life | general purpose (default of `gna_verifier_pq()`); GloBI |
| `4` | NCBI | `tax_retroblast_pq()`; NCBI/SILVA-like lineages |
| `5` | Index Fungorum | fungal trait databases (`fungal_traits_guilds()`) |
| `11` | GBIF Backbone Taxonomy | GBIF functions with the `"backbone"` checklist, `tax_iucn_code_pq()`, `tax_photos_pq()` |
| `13` | Catalogue of Life XR | GBIF functions with the `"colxr"` checklist (rgbif >= 3.9.0) |
| `207` | Wikidata | Wikipedia / Wikidata functions |
| `208` | LPSN | bacterial names (BactoTraits) |
| `210` | TaxRef | French databases (TAXREF, its `CD_NOM` / `CD_REF` with `id_col = TRUE`) |
